R e s p o n d e n t s _____________

_ _ For Insurance Company : Mr. Anumeh Shrivastava and Mr. Akash Shrivastava, Advocates (MAC No.511/15) : Mr.
Praveen Dhurandhar, Advocate For Respondents (MAC No.511/15) : Mr. Ashwell Franklin, Advocate appears on behalf of Mr. Samir Singh, Advocate Hon'ble Shri Justice Arvind Singh Chandel Order On Board 11/08/2023 1.

Both the appeals have arisen out of award dated 31.01.2015, passed by Additional Motor Accident Claim Tribunal (FTC), Dhamtari, District Dhamtari (C.G.) (hereinafter referred to as 'the Claims Tribunal'), therefore, the same are deciding by this common order.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Facts of the cases are that on 30.10.2011, around 2:30 PM, deceased Ganeshwar was traveling with his younger brother Parmeshwar in his motor cycle bearing Registration No.CG 05 C 4110 and when they reached near C.G. Rice Mills, Village Sambalpur, they were hit by a jeep bearing Registration No. CG 05 ZA 2028 (hereinafter referred to as 'the offending vehicle'), which was driven by driver Kapoor Ram Soni who was driving the offending vehicle rashly and negligently due to that Ganeshwar died on spot and Parmeshwar received grievous injuries.

Legal heirs of Ganeshwar filed a claim petition which was registered as claim case No.13/13 and injured Parmeshwar filed a separate claim petition which was registered as claim case No.14/13 under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act before the Claims Tribunal.

3. After recording the evidence of both parties and after hearing learned Counsels appearing for the parties, the Claims Tribunal has passed a common order dated 31.01.2015 and passed an award of Rs.28,429/- in favour of injured Parmeshwar and also passed an award of Rs. 4,43,000/- in favour of legal heirs of Ganeshwar and fastened the liability on Insurance Company.
Hence, these appeals have been preferred by the Insurance Company.

4. Learned Counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that at the time of accident, the offending vehicle was used as passenger carrying vehicle and at the time of incident, no permit and fitness was available in the offending vehicle, therefore, there was a breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
Hence, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation.

Further, as the Insurance Company has pleaded in its written statement that no permit and fitness was available in the offending vehicle and the driver/owner of the offending vehicle was required to prove that the vehicle had permit and fitness but, no evidence has been produced by the Oriental Insurance Company Ltd vs Parmeshwar And Ors on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93408109/
2 driver/owner of the offending vehicle in this regard before the Claims Tribunal and the Claims Tribunal has wrongly fastened the liability on Insurance Company and passed the impugned award.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Learned Counsel appearing for the Respondents/Claimants submit that there was no pleading by the Insurance Company that the offending vehicle was used as passenger carrying vehicle at the time of accident, therefore, necessity of permit was not required.
Hence, the Claims Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability on Insurance Company.
6. I have heard learned Counsel appearing for the parties and perused the entire material available on record with utmost circumspection.

7. On careful perusal of the written statement submitted by the Insurance Company shows that there was no pleading by the Insurance Company that at the time of accident the offending vehicle was used as passenger carrying vehicle and passengers were traveling in the offending vehicle.
It also appears that none of the witnesses have stated anything in this regard.

Therefore, it is well established that there was no pleading by the Insurance Company that the offending vehicle was used as passenger carrying vehicle and at the time of accident passengers were seated in the offending vehicle.
Therefore, necessity of permit was not required.
Thus, the Claims Tribunal has rightly fastened the liability on the Insurance Company.
8. I do not find any merits in these appeals and the same are liable to be and are hereby dismissed.
